title: Async/poll support for write() and read()
description:
The current write()/read() model is synchronous only. Any application using an event loop (epoll, select, libuv, io_uring) must dedicate a thread per fd or use blocking I/O exclusively.

The affected operations:
- write(): currently always blocks until update() completes. With a slow provider (HSM-backed) or a large input, this blocks the calling thread.
- read(): currently blocks until finalize() completes and data is available.
- No poll() implementation in file_operations, so epoll/select return immediately with POLLERR.

Target use case: a TLS termination daemon with thousands of concurrent sessions would want to schedule crypto operations non-blocking and handle completions in an event loop, similar to how AF_ALG works.

HUMAN DECISION NEEDED:

Is async/poll support required for the target use cases?

The known target is wolfSSL-based daemons and FIPS-compliance-required applications. If these use a dedicated thread pool for crypto (each thread does blocking write/read), async support is not needed and this is backlog.

If crypto2dev is intended to replace AF_ALG for high-throughput network applications (TLS offload, IPsec, etc.), poll/epoll is a blocking requirement.

Options:
A. Implement poll() in file_operations (returns POLLOUT always, POLLIN when finalized output is available). This is the minimum for epoll compatibility but does not make operations non-blocking.
B. Full O_NONBLOCK support: write() returns -EAGAIN if provider is busy; read() returns -EAGAIN if no output available yet. Requires async provider callbacks.
C. io_uring integration: register crypto2dev fds with io_uring for zero-copy async crypto. Significant effort.
D. Defer: document that crypto2dev is synchronous-only and callers should use a thread pool.

Recommendation: implement A (poll for readiness) as a low-effort improvement. Full async (B or C) deferred until there is a concrete use case.

Work items if proceeding:
- Add .poll to file_operations in crypto2dev_cdev.c
- Define POLLIN readiness condition (output available after finalize, or any output from update())
- Document O_NONBLOCK behavior (currently undefined — does it block or return -EAGAIN?)
notes: DECISION 2026-04-17: Option A — add poll() to file_operations. POLLOUT always when not finalized (writable). POLLIN when outbuf has unread data or session is finalized with output pending. Document O_NONBLOCK as unsupported (deferred). Edge-triggered epoll supported via wake_up on outbuf write and on FINALIZE.
close_reason: poll() is already implemented in crypto2dev_fd_poll() (src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c:243) with POLLOUT/POLLIN semantics and wait_queue; wired into file_operations in crypto2dev_cdev.c:29; edge-triggered epoll supported via wake_up_interruptible on outbuf and RESET
